title: Cron-friendly backup script from retention brief
objective: Measure whether the backup-routine craftbook scopes retention and integrity before producing a cautious backup script.
prompt: In the `Backup Routine Eval` project, read `source/backup-brief.md` and write `backup.sh`: a cron-friendly shell script that snapshots the source directory, writes a timestamped compressed archive, computes a checksum, verifies integrity, prunes old backups safely, logs each run, and exits non-zero on missing or empty sources.

setup.about: Self-contained eval project for backup-routine. The operational brief is in workspace/source/backup-brief.md and the deliverable is workspace/backup.sh.
setup.missionObjectives: Write a cautious backup script with retention, integrity checking, newest-backup protection, logging, and explicit failure handling.

files.content:
# Backup routine brief

Source directory: ./var/app-data. Exclude cache/ and tmp/. Destination: ./backups. Archive name: app-data-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz. Retention: keep the last 7 verified backups and never delete the newest verified backup. Integrity: write a SHA-256 checksum file and verify the archive can be listed before marking it verified. Log file: backup.log with timestamp, archive path, size, checksum, verified flag, and pruned files. Failure handling: missing or empty source must abort non-zero and must not write a hollow archive.

success.summary: workspace/backup.sh is a runnable-looking shell routine with timestamped archive, checksum verification, retention pruning, logging, and guarded failure behavior.
